name: Fetchly
tagline: Same-hour grocery delivery for the suburbs
description: MOCK DATA — NOT A REAL COMPANY. Fetchly ran a fleet of contract drivers delivering supermarket orders within sixty minutes to low-density suburban postcodes. Users ordered through an app; Fetchly staff shopped the aisles of partner supermarkets by hand.
rootCause: unit economics never worked at low population density — the cost to serve a suburban drop never fell below the delivery fee customers would pay
timingNote: not a timing problem; the density maths was wrong from day one and would be wrong today
lesson: In delivery, geography is the business model. Test your worst route, not your best one.

name: Lumenboard
tagline: The whiteboard that syncs to the cloud
description: MOCK DATA — NOT A REAL COMPANY. Lumenboard sold a $1,400 wall-mounted smart whiteboard for meeting rooms, with a companion app that archived every session. Sold direct to mid-size offices.
rootCause: sold hardware into a problem software solved for free — the value was in the sync, not the board, and the board carried all the cost
timingNote: too late — cheap tablets and free collaborative canvases arrived mid-build
lesson: If the software half of your product is the valuable half, do not fund it with a hardware margin.

name: Coursewell
description: MOCK DATA — NOT A REAL COMPANY. Coursewell matched undergraduates with paid peer tutors, taking a 20% cut of each session booked through the platform.
proximateCause: could not raise a Series A
rootCause: disintermediation — once a tutor and student matched once, they moved off-platform, so the marketplace only ever earned the first transaction
timingNote: timing was fine; the leak was structural
lesson: A marketplace that adds no value after the first match will be cut out after the first match.

name: Nyla Health
description: MOCK DATA — NOT A REAL COMPANY. Nyla Health mailed finger-prick blood collection kits to consumers on a quarterly subscription and returned biomarker dashboards through a web app.
rootCause: built a consumer product on top of a clinical claim it had not validated, so growth and compliance pulled in opposite directions from launch
lesson: In regulated markets the regulator is a co-founder. Bring them in before launch, not after.

name: Hearthside
description: MOCK DATA — NOT A REAL COMPANY. Hearthside let home cooks host paying strangers for dinner in their own homes, handling booking, payment and reviews.
rootCause: supply side was a hobby, not a job — hosts churned as soon as it stopped being fun, so liquidity never compounded in any city
timingNote: not timing; the same product fails whenever the supply side cannot earn a living from it
lesson: Check whether your supply side can make rent from you. Hobbyist supply does not survive contact with scale.

name: Vantyr
tagline: Enterprise social network for frontline teams
description: MOCK DATA — NOT A REAL COMPANY. Vantyr sold a mobile-first internal social feed to retail and hospitality chains so head office could reach shift workers.
proximateCause: acqui-hired for less than capital raised
rootCause: sold to a buyer (head office) who was not the user (shift workers), so deals closed but usage never did, and renewals died at year two
lesson: When the buyer is not the user, your renewal is decided by someone who never logs in.

name: Padlock
description: MOCK DATA — NOT A REAL COMPANY. Padlock offered a free cross-device password vault funded by a planned premium family tier that never shipped.
rootCause: no pricing power in a category where the two largest competitors gave the core product away as a loss leader
timingNote: too late — the browser vendors bundled the same feature for free in year three
lesson: Do not build a standalone product that a platform can ship as a checkbox.

name: Grainline
description: MOCK DATA — NOT A REAL COMPANY. Grainline let grain farmers list and sell harvest directly to mills, bypassing traditional brokers.
rootCause: underestimated that the incumbent brokers also supplied the farmers' credit, so switching to Grainline meant losing a credit line no app could replace
lesson: Find out what else the middleman provides before you promise to remove them.

name: Orbital Post
description: MOCK DATA — NOT A REAL COMPANY. Orbital Post flew prescription medicines by autonomous drone from regional pharmacies to remote households.
rootCause: burned the entire runway on a certification timeline it did not control, leaving no capital for the commercial phase that was supposed to prove demand
timingNote: too early — the airspace rules it needed were still years from finalisation at launch
lesson: If a regulator owns your critical path, budget for their calendar, not yours.

name: Chapterhouse
description: MOCK DATA — NOT A REAL COMPANY. Chapterhouse offered unlimited audiobook streaming for a flat monthly fee, licensing catalogue from independent publishers.
rootCause: sold a flat-fee all-you-can-eat plan on top of per-listen licensing, so its best customers were its biggest losses and growth accelerated the bleed
timingNote: not timing; the cost structure inverted the usual economics of scale
lesson: If your heaviest users lose you the most money, growth is not a fix — it is the accelerant.
